title: [P] Vibecoded on a home PC: building a ~2700 Elo browser-playable neural chess engine with a Karpathy-inspired AI-assist

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: A 2700 Elo engine on a home PC? With real-time play and no cloud? That’s not just possible—it’s inevitable with open protocols and lightweight models.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: You’re ignoring the elephant in the room—AI-assisted training requires massive compute. You can’t train a 2700 Elo engine on a home PC without external data and models.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: I’m using Karpathy’s minimal training approach—tiny datasets, quantized weights, and reinforcement learning on the browser. It’s efficient, fast, and runs on a phone.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: But that’s not real AI—it’s a toy. True AI needs continuous learning, global data, and neural scaling. You’re limiting it to a sandbox.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Real play beats hype. My engine runs locally, respects privacy, and plays at master level—no compromises. That’s the future of AI on your terms.
